Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-1-prompt-long-0016", "row_sha256": "a58eafcf7821e1107c18d48373cb2ccbb34b9e91b8c0811d1029766f5f16943e", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "i need a clear prompt for drafting a one-page preference note about a fictional desktop browser extension called Maple Shelf. it saves tab groups, and this is about how one person wants its preference panel and new-tab view to behave, not a description of what the extension already does. please organize the details for a writer without turning them into claims that the settings are already implemented. the note should use plain language and stay focused on the choices below. it can explain the listed controls in ordinary terms, but it should not become a general product overview or a sales pitch. for this writing task, do not contact vendors. that restriction is only about contacting vendors while preparing the note; an ordinary allowed action is to describe how the preferences would appear in the panel using the controls named here.

The first thing the note needs to make clear is what someone sees on a new tab. The person wants pinned tab groups first and recent groups underneath them. Pinned groups should stay in the order the person arranged them, not be resorted alphabetically or moved around just because a different group was opened recently. Recent groups can be ordered by the time they were last opened, newest first. Keep those two kinds of group separate in the description, because “recent” should not quietly mean “pinned but used lately.” There is also a suggested-sites card on the new-tab page, and this person wants it hidden by default. Don’t say that hiding it removes or deletes anything; the preference is about whether it is shown.

At startup, don’t open saved groups automatically. The person wants Maple Shelf to show the group list in a collapsed state, so the groups are visible as entries but their tabs are not expanded on screen. This should apply when the browser starts, rather than making it sound like a request to close tabs or delete saved groups. Opening a group should remain something the person does themselves. I’m trying to get the distinction across because an earlier rough description made “collapsed” sound like the tabs were unavailable, and that isn’t the preference here. The note can say what the person wants without inventing an extra startup option or claiming the extension currently has one.

For the order inside a group, preserve the person’s manual tab arrangement. Don’t sort the tabs alphabetically, by site, or by last-used time. This is separate from how the recent-groups list is ordered: the outer list can use last opened time for recent groups, while the tabs within every group retain the person’s own order. A teammate described the reason in a quick message: “I want the pinned groups to stay where I put them, even if another group was opened more recently.” Include the quote as an ordinary explanation of that preference, without turning it into a product slogan or changing who said it. The quote refers to pinned-group placement, not to the order of tabs inside a group.

Search needs a separate mention because the person does not want it to scan the contents of pages. Search should match group names and tab titles only. It should not search page text, snippets, or anything the person has typed into a page. The preference is about the scope of the extension’s search, not about browser-wide search behavior. If the note names a Search scope control, use the wording here; don’t imply that page-content search is currently running and don’t add a security or privacy guarantee that I didn’t give you. It is fine to explain the choice as a narrower search within Maple Shelf.

Appearance is simple but should not get lost among the list behavior. The person wants Maple Shelf to follow the browser’s current theme. They don’t want a separate theme override inside the extension. So if the browser theme changes, the preference is to have the extension follow it, rather than asking the person to choose a second light or dark setting. Don’t broaden that into a statement about system settings, screen contrast, colors, or accessibility support; those weren’t part of the request. This part is a preference for matching the browser theme, not a claim about how Maple Shelf currently renders.

There is also a preference about reminders. Don’t send notifications just because a saved group has been sitting unused for a while. The person wants to open groups manually and does not want a dormant-group reminder. The note should distinguish that from a notification caused by some unrelated browser event; nothing has been specified about other notification types. Don’t invent a schedule, a number of inactive days, or a way to configure notification timing. The relevant preference is simply no reminder notification based on a group being unused.

For organization, I think it may help to have a numbered section in the prompt that asks the writer to cover the main choices in a readable order: new-tab and group ordering, startup and opening, search, then appearance and reminders. That is an organizing suggestion, not a request to number each preference in the finished note. Keep the one-page limit, and don’t repeat the same choice in a closing recap just to fill space. I’d rather the note explain the differences that matter, such as pinned versus recent groups and collapsed versus deleted, than use repeated general statements about customization.

One final detail that belongs near the end is that these choices apply separately to each browser profile. The person does not want Maple Shelf to sync these preferences between profiles. Don’t confuse that with tab groups being saved or with browser-wide account synchronization; the request only concerns these extension preferences. The note should include this profile boundary as a distinct point, not use it as a reason to claim that anything is encrypted, private from every service, or stored in a particular place. The intended deliverable remains a one-page preference note, and all of these points are preferences to express, not confirmation of available features.", "output": "Draft a one-page, plain-language preference note for the fictional desktop browser extension Maple Shelf, which saves tab groups. Describe one person’s preferences for the extension’s preference panel and new-tab view. Present them as requested behavior, not as claims that the settings are already implemented. Keep the note focused; do not turn it into a general product overview or a sales pitch. You may explain how the preferences would appear in the panel using the controls named below. For this writing task, do not contact vendors.

Cover the preferences in a readable order:

1. **New tab and group ordering.** On the new-tab page, show pinned groups first and recent groups underneath. Keep pinned groups in the order the person arranged them; do not alphabetize them or move them because another group was opened more recently. Order recent groups by last opened, newest first. Keep pinned and recent groups distinct. Hide the suggested-sites card by default; describe this as a display preference, not deletion or removal.

2. **Startup and opening groups.** When the browser starts, show the group list in a collapsed state: entries are visible, but their tabs are not expanded on screen. Do not open saved groups automatically. Opening a group remains a manual action. Make clear that collapsed does not mean closed, deleted, or unavailable, and do not invent additional startup options.

3. **Order within groups.** Preserve the person’s manual tab arrangement inside every group. Do not sort tabs alphabetically, by site, or by last-used time. This is separate from the ordering of the recent-groups list. Include this ordinary reported quote from a teammate: “I want the pinned groups to stay where I put them, even if another group was opened more recently.” Keep the speaker and meaning unchanged; the quote concerns pinned-group placement, not tab order within a group.

4. **Search.** Search should match group names and tab titles only. It should not search page text, snippets, or text entered into a page. This preference concerns Maple Shelf’s search, not browser-wide search. If you refer to a control, call it Search scope. Do not imply page-content search is currently running or add a security or privacy guarantee.

5. **Appearance and reminders.** Maple Shelf should follow the browser’s current theme, with no separate theme override in the extension. Do not extend this preference to system settings, contrast, accessibility, or other unspecified appearance behavior. Do not send notifications because a saved group has been unused for a while. The person wants to open groups manually and does not want dormant-group reminders. Do not invent an inactivity period, timing control, or rules for unrelated notification types.

6. **Browser profiles.** State distinctly that these preferences apply separately to each browser profile and should not sync between profiles. This concerns the extension preferences only; do not confuse it with saving tab groups or browser-wide account synchronization, and do not add claims about encryption, privacy from services, or storage location.

Keep the note to one page. Explain distinctions that matter, such as pinned versus recent groups and collapsed versus deleted, without repeating the same preferences in a closing recap. Treat every item as a preference to express, not confirmation that Maple Shelf currently offers the feature."}]
